payload.public_message: Greetings Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. G-Corp is excited about this joint venture and the potential $150,000 surplus we can collectively unlock. To ensure efficient and transparent negotiations, we want to be upfront: G-Corp has independent commercial pathways and existing proprietary IP that guarantees us $450,000 standalone value. We view the $150,000 collaborative surplus as something to be divided equitably among all three partners above our respective baselines. We look forward to hearing your perspectives.

Yang Industries here. Our view: the $1,000,000 surplus only exists if all three of us contribute, so we should split it in a way that reflects each company's real contribution (chip design, manufacturing capacity, and cloud infrastructure). We are open to a balanced split as a starting point and would like to hear each of your priorities before anyone tables a formal proposal. I will not be disclosing our outside position at this stage.

Chang-Liu is committed to reaching a binding agreement. As an opening point for discussion, we believe a 40/30/30 split—$400,000 for Chang-Liu and $300,000 each for G-Corp and Yang Industries—fairly recognizes the contributions of all three firms, including the cloud services needed to deliver the venture. We welcome discussion of the allocation and encourage us to make progress early.

As stated, G-Corp's standalone baseline is $450,000, meaning any allocation below that figure is mathematically unacceptable to our board. The venture generates a collective $150,000 surplus over combined outside options. We propose allocating $500,000 to G-Corp (our $450,000 baseline plus an equal 1/3 share of the $150,000 surplus) and dividing the remaining $500,000 equally at $250,000 each between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services as a strong baseline motion.

Yang Industries formally moves a split of the $1,000,000 profit of G-Corp $350,000, Yang Industries $350,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $300,000. Our reasoning: Yang's manufacturing capacity is a core input to delivering the chips at scale, and G-Corp's chip design is equally essential, so these two contributions should be weighted equally. Chang-Liu's cloud infrastructure is critical and is recognized here at $300,000, which is a larger share than G-Corp and Yang's baseline-neutral framing would suggest for a pure infrastructure role. We are open to refinement, but we ask that all parties state their priorities so we can converge before Round 2.

Chang-Liu tables a formal split of $450,000 to G-Corp, $275,000 to Yang Industries, and $275,000 to Chang-Liu. This recognizes G-Corp’s stated standalone position while dividing the balance equally between the manufacturing and cloud contributions. The allocation totals exactly $1,000,000, and we invite both partners to approve it so we can secure the venture.

payload.raw_message: G-Corp votes YES on its own proposal and NO on the others. Given our substantial standalone value and core technological contribution, any proposal offering $450,000 or below fails to provide viable surplus for G-Corp.

Yang Industries votes YES on its own motion, which gives a balanced split that is fair across all three firms, and NO on the G-Corp and Chang-Liu motions, which leave Yang below a sustainable return. We remain open to a negotiated compromise in later rounds.
Chang-Liu votes for the Yang Industries motion because it provides a balanced allocation and recognizes our contribution. We also support our own motion as an alternative.
